title: Evaluation checks that restate data or enter below the family entry are removed

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-396#remove-redundant-evaluation-checks, Slice 3 (plan 680)
Revision: d6cae1e36d5d307071c61c419852c21d42227bf2 (branch claude/evaluation-checks-that-restate-data-or-enter-bel). Slice 3 commit: 3660bdadc.

Promise under test
"A check is removed only if it restates data or configuration, repeats the same scenario, or has a named retained/replacement entry-level check that fails on a break of its covered behavior." Applied to Slice 3: the 12-case `native_case_known delivery-evidence/<name>` loop and the two `delivery_evidence_case_has_scenario drift ...` checks were removed from delivery-evidence-native-routing.sh. What should still be observable: the real publication entry accepts each registered delivery case and refuses an unknown one.

Fault (I checked the suggested one and corrected its path)
- File: Distribution/evaluation/cases/git-publication/git-publication-native-host.sh. The suggestion said `src/`; the function is under `cases/`.
- Function: `native_case_known`, line 165, just before the generic `delivery-evidence/*)` arm.
- Change: inserted `delivery-evidence/selection) return 1 ;;`. The router then rejects one registered case that the dispatch loop never sends. Fixtures and assertions were not touched.
- Process note: my first attempt used a regex that hit the earlier `delivery-evidence/*)` arm in `run_native_host` (line 71), so the fault landed in the wrong place. That run proves nothing and I discarded it. Separately, with that misplaced fault the real entry passed validation and returned 1 at the injected arm, before `delivery_evidence_run_journey`. No host started and no paid run happened. I restored the file and reapplied the fault at the correct line. Before every later entry run I first confirmed through the sourced function that the fault was in place, and put sentinel codex/claude/cursor binaries first on PATH.

Showing the behavior actually broke (independent of the tests)
- Before the fault: sourcing the router and calling `native_case_known delivery-evidence/selection` returned 0.
- With the fault: the same call returned 1, while `delivery-evidence/drift` still returned 0.
- Real entry with the fault: `bash Distribution/evaluation/cases/git-publication/git-publication-native.sh --native codex --case delivery-evidence/selection` exited 2 with "error: unknown native case 'delivery-evidence/selection'". So the real entry refuses a valid registered case. The sentinel log was absent, so no host started.

Checks run (scratch worktree; command was `env PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_JOBS=2 caffeinate -s -i bash scripts/test.sh <paths>`)
- Distribution/evaluation/tests/delivery-evidence/delivery-evidence-native-routing.sh (the focused check)
- Distribution/evaluation/tests/delivery-evidence/proof-scheduling-native.sh (the focused check)
- Distribution/evaluation/tests/git-publication/git-publication-native-entry.sh (nearest entry check; it only uses `publication/publish-boundary`)

Results
- Baseline: exit 0, about 95 s wall. This run did not record per-job outcomes. The restored run below did record each job passing.
- With the fault: exit 0, about 103 s wall. All three jobs reported `passed`.
- What reached the faulted path: the routing test calls the real entry only with `delivery-evidence/missing` (still refused) and `native_case_known` only with `delivery-evidence/drift` (still accepted). The dispatch loop calls `run_native_host` for gaps, original, terminal, release, drift and amended. That path uses `delivery_evidence_case_known` directly and never goes through `native_case_known`. No maintained check among these three reached the broken transition.
- Pre-Slice-3 routing test under the same fault: I put a scratch copy of `3660bdadc^`'s file next to the test and ran it. It exited 1 at `native_case_known delivery-evidence/selection` (seen in the bash -x trace). The removed loop would have caught this fault.
- Restoration: copied the original file back and removed the probe copy. `git status --porcelain` was empty, matching the clean state before the probe. `native_case_known delivery-evidence/selection` returned 0 again. The same command exited 0 with all three jobs `passed`, about 81 s wall. The scratch worktree was then removed with `git worktree remove --force`. The execution checkout was never modified and is still clean.

Verdict: Confirmed missing test path, bounded to the three checks examined.
The router refusing a registered delivery case that is not dispatched breaks the promised behavior: the real entry refuses a valid case. delivery-evidence-native-routing.sh, proof-scheduling-native.sh and git-publication-native-entry.sh all pass and never take that path. The missing transition is "the real entry, or `native_case_known`, accepts each registered delivery-evidence case". After Slice 3 it is checked only for `drift`.

How the story would classify the lost check
- The removed loop copied the registry's 12 case names into the test, so by the story's wording it is a restated inventory. The plan's audit row says to prune "the all-case and fixed scenario inventories". The plan also says the scratch "establishes no replacement" for them, and it names no replacement.
- What the loop actually observed was router acceptance, which is behavior, not just data. Because the router has a generic `delivery-evidence/*` passthrough, the only fault it uniquely catches is a case-specific mis-arm like this one, which is fairly contrived. A broken passthrough as a whole would still fail the retained `drift` query.
- So the removal fits the story's "restates data" rule, but some narrow protection was lost. The probe shows it was unique within the examined checks.
- The story requires "selection refusals". Refusing an invalid case is still covered by the retained `delivery-evidence/missing` entry check. This fault goes the other way: a valid case is refused.

Next proof action (for the caller to decide)
If per-case acceptance is worth keeping, add a check that loops over the live registry (`${delivery_evidence_cases}`) instead of a copied list and asserts that `native_case_known` or the real entry accepts each case. It must stop before any host launch. That keeps the protection without restating data. If the caller decides this narrow mis-arm is not worth protecting, nothing is needed. This is a new decision raised by the probe, not a repair already in the plan.

Costs
- Test runtime: measured, wall seconds of the `scripts/test.sh` invocation (3 jobs, 2 slots, machine load 23–30). Baseline 95 s; misplaced-fault run (discarded) 119 s; real fault 103 s; restored 81 s. Total about 398 s. Per-job runner times for the fault run: proof-scheduling 102.5 s, routing 39.5 s, entry 27.6 s. Restored run: 81.2 s, 30.9 s, 22.1 s.
- Human effort: unavailable. Terry was not involved during the probe, and there is no separate measure of his time.
- Agent effort: estimated, about 15 agent tool calls in one subagent session. Token counts were not available to the agent.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 536007 ms (measured), from 1794920085743 to 1794920621750 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision d6cae1e36d5d307071c61c419852c21d42227bf2. Verdict: confirmed missing test path for per-case router acceptance of non-dispatched delivery cases. Decision: no follow-up. The lost loop copied the registry's case names, which the story explicitly removes as restated data; the router accepts every delivery case through one generic `delivery-evidence/*` arm, which the retained `drift` query still exercises, so only a deliberately added case-specific refusal arm escapes, and that would be a visible code change. Recorded as process finding DD-563.
